author: Chris Pinson
title: Irish fall to Tigers in Class 4 State Semifinals - NewsBreak
text:
By Chris Pinson ,
1 hours ago
OZARK–The Springfield Catholic baseball team will collect their 10th overall trophy from participating in the Class 4 State playoffs, on Thursday, but it’ll come from finishing in third or fourth place, not firsr or second.
The Irish fell 2-0 to Excelsior Springs in the State Semifinals, on Wednesday. Both teams entered the game averaging 8 runs a game, however, both starting pitchers were lights out on the mound.
Catholic starter, Jack Smith, who’s committed to pitch for Drury University next spring, recovered from Tommy John surgery during his junior year, in time for his senior season, only allowed two hits and one earned run, while striking out seven Tigers hitters in six innings of work.
Unfortunately, the Irish offense just couldn’t bring home the small village they left on base to provide any run support for Smith.
In the top of the first, Catholic had the bases loaded and a chance to take control from the jump, but a groundout to short ended the inning before they could plate a runner. Then, in the top of the third, after falling behind 2-0, Irish had runners on second and third without no outs, but after Nate Lask grounded out to the pitcher, overzealous base running lead to Sam Boster getting caught in a rundown between third and home, and was tagged out trying to score.
Those missed opportunities could’ve made all the difference for Catholic’s title hopes.
“I told our guys at the end of the day, we just didn’t come up with the big hit when we had runners on,” said Irish Head Coach, Courtney Spitz. “We out hit them. Jack Smith was amazing on the mound today, super efficient. It’s just the tough part of sports. Tough part of baseball. Anybody can win, on any day. Their pitcher was really good, credit to him. We had chances, we just didn’t get that big hit.”
Catholic will play Westminster Christian in the third-and-fourth place game Thursday, at 10 a.m.
